Based on the image provided, here is the precise description of the view:

**Main Content Area (Reusable Workflows)**
*   **List Title:** "Reusable workflows"
*   **Subtitle:** "Successful steps, saved so you can run them again"
*   **Empty State Title:** "No reusable workflows yet"
*   **Empty State Body Text:** "A reusable workflow remembers the successful steps of a task — exactly what ran — so you can run them again on a new task any time."
*   **Guidance on Saving:** Under the heading "What to do next", the text reads: "Finish a task successfully, then choose “Save as a reusable workflow” on it — the saved workflow appears here."

**Navigation / Sidebar State**
The left sidebar displays the following structure and state:
*   **Top Level Items:** New chat, Repository, Pull requests, Plugins, and **Workflows** (which appears to be the active parent category).
*   **Workspace Section:**
    *   Projects & tasks
    *   **Reusable workflows** (This item is highlighted with a light grey background, indicating it is the currently selected view).
    *   Artifacts
    *   Activity
*   **Projects Section:**
    *   A project named "**seed-ws**" is expanded.
    *   Inside this project, there is an active task titled "**Wave 3 gate anchor task**" marked as "**now**".
*   **Chats Section:** Displays "No chats".
*   **Bottom Section:** Terminal, Browser, Settings, and a status indicator showing "App-server online".

**Other Visible Elements**
*   **Top Bar:** Standard window controls (minimize, maximize, close) and menu items (File, Edit, View, Help). There is also a "Back to your work" link in the top right of the content area.
*   **Footer/Toast Notification:** A banner at the bottom states: "This task is up to date — there's nothing to pick up right now." with a "Dismiss" button.
